claim: *Behavioral models expose different classes of properties.* A transition relation can support local legality checks, reasoning over reachable states, or temporal claims over executions. The appropriate checker follows from the property; richer machinery is not automatically stronger for every question.

topology.description: One behavioral model forks to three property/checker questions that converge on behavioral evidence.

required_terms: Behavioral model States · transitions · legal sequences
Local rule Is this edge legal? Transition check
Reachable-state Can this state occur? State-space search
Temporal property Will this eventually occur? Temporal model checking
bw_encoding: Black outlines and arrows; white nodes; sparse 3–7% gray groups. Every non-solid relation is locally labeled; no distinction depends on color.
redesign: Native semantic redraw; colors replaced by labeled relations and line conventions.
alt: One behavioral model branches to three questions: whether an edge is legal, whether a state is reachable and whether a temporal property holds. Transition checking, state-space search and temporal model checking supply corresponding behavioral evidence. The candidate uses black lines, white backgrounds and sparse gray; meaning does not depend on color.
